oneOf.description: Tap a selector or a point.
Type text, optionally into a selected node first.
Wait for a selector (event-driven, not a polling sleep).

fresh_frame.description: Produce a fresh frame as part of the assertion evidence.

Assertion.description: Any assertion the `assert` command can evaluate.

timeout_ms.description: Event-driven timeout; the runtime waits for a matching frame/tree, never for a fixed sleep.

min_matches.description: Minimum number of matched lines required per pattern.

patterns.description: Regex patterns to match against log messages.

since_previous_step.description: Only consider log events produced since the previous scenario step. This is what makes lifecycle assertions step-scoped instead of matching an earlier cycle.

tag.description: Log tag to filter on (for example `AcosFixture`).

baseline.description: Baseline PNG path, relative to the scenario file or workspace root.

tolerance.description: Maximum allowed fraction of changed pixels in `0.0..=1.0`.

Bounds.description:
Integer screen bounds `[left, top, right, bottom]` in pixels.

Serialized as a four-element array. `right`/`bottom` are exclusive at the Android/UI-automator pixel-grid level.

CapabilityReportRequest.description: `capability-report`: what this engine can do for an APK/scenario.

after_cause.description: Only accept a frame caused by this request/action id.

after_seq.description: Only accept a frame with `frame_seq > after_seq`.

fresh.description: Require a frame produced after the request (default true).

output.description: Output path, relative to the artifacts directory.

DataPolicy.description: Data lifetime policy for a new session.

oneOf.description: Fresh app data, discarded on destroy.
Fresh app data, kept until reset.

DisplaySpec.description:
The display a session renders to.

`none` is headless: capture/observe must return `NO_DISPLAY` instead of silently allocating a surface.

oneOf.description: No display at all (headless logic/storage tests).
Offscreen software surface with an explicit size and density.

density_dpi.description: Density in dots per inch (for example 420).

EventKind.description: The event kinds an agent can filter on.

oneOf.description: Acknowledgement that an input action was delivered.

since_seq.description: Return events with `seq > since_seq` (cursor from the previous call).

timeout_ms.description: Event-driven wait for at least one matching event.

Fidelity.description:
How faithful the execution behind a result is.

* `static-analysis` — host parsing only. Proves nothing about runtime behaviour. * `jvm-reference` — host OpenJDK. Proves pure-Java semantics only; never Android/ART/framework/JNI/rendering behaviour. * `native-runtime` — executed by ACOS itself (its Rust VM/loader/renderer). This is **not** validated against ART unless `validated_against` says so. * `art-reference` — real ART on a reference Android image. Authoritative for Android framework behaviour at the stated API/ABI. * `physical-device` — a real device/OEM target. * `simulated` — a mock/stub path. A simulated success is not an Android success. * `n/a` — a **meta** reply: a tool that reports on ACOS itself (`acos_help`, `acos_capabilities`, `acos_doctor`). It says nothing about app behaviour, so labelling it `static-analysis` would imply the reply was derived from the APK. `n/a` never satisfies a fidelity requirement and is never a pass.

oneOf.description: ACOS native execution; not ART-validated by itself.
Not applicable: a meta reply about ACOS itself (help/capabilities/doctor).

IsolationLevel.description:
How independent a session is from other sessions.

The levels are ordered from cheapest/weakest to strongest. A claim of data independence is only allowed at `sandbox` and above, and only when the engine actually implements the guarantees (see `docs/AGENT_API.md`).

oneOf.description: Another activity/task in a shared process and shared app data. No isolation.
Separate process, potentially the same package/storage identity.
Separate process/UID/credentials/mount namespace and app data.
Fully separate engine instance (strongest short of a VM).
Sandboxed full Android/backend for untrusted or device-level fidelity.

ObserveRequest.description: `observe`: UI tree, text and frame metadata.

max_nodes.description: Maximum nodes to return (truncation is reported).

png.description:
Capture this frame's PNG into the reply (`true`).

The ART daemon writes it under the session's artifacts and reports the path (same as `screenshot: true`); the Flutter route returns the PNG inline (`png_base64`/`png_bytes`). A route that cannot produce pixels answers `UNSUPPORTED_BACKEND` instead of a reply that silently has none.

screenshot.description:
Write this frame's PNG (`true` = under the session's artifacts and return the path; a string = that destination inside the artifacts directory).

The pixels are always those of the frame the tree in the same reply describes; a placeholder/no-pixel frame is `NO_FRESH_FRAME`, never an empty success.

RegionMask.description:
A rectangle excluded from screenshot comparison (clock, status bar, ...).

Bounds are **display pixels**, like every other rectangle in the scenario format; the executor maps them onto the frame with the frame's `display_origin`.

reason.description: Why this region is nondeterministic (documented, not decorative).

RequestBase.description: Identity fields present on every request.

cause_id.description: The cause of the last known frame, when relevant.

frame_seq.description: The last frame sequence the client has seen, when relevant.

request_id.description: Client-chosen request id, echoed in the envelope and used as the frame `cause_id` for actions that produce a frame.

session_id.description: Session the request targets (absent for session-creating commands).

oneOf.description: Recreate the task only; app data is shared.

ResourceBudget.description:
Hard resource budgets for one request or one scenario.

Every field is opt-in; `None` means "use the engine default". The engine must return `RESOURCE_LIMIT`/`TIMEOUT` when a budget is exhausted instead of silently exceeding it.

memory_mib.description: Maximum resident memory attributable to this request/session, in MiB.

RunRequest.description: `run`: launch an app and create a session.

base.description: Identity fields; `isolation` and `display` are honoured here.

intent_action.description: Intent action instead of an explicit activity.

name.description: Human label for the session (also used in artifacts).

Selector.description: A node selector. See the module docs for the stable matching rules.

hint.description: Hint matcher (`TextView.getHint()`, e.g. an EditText placeholder).

id.description: Android resource id (`pkg:id/name`), or a bare local id (`name`).

include_invisible.description:
Also match nodes that are not visible to the user.

Default `false`: a selector matches only nodes the user can see (`UiNode::visible`, which follows `View.isVisibleToUser()`: shown, and its clipped visible rect non-empty). A warm-mounted page parked off screen is present in the tree but is not a selector match, so `wait_for`/`assert_text`/`assert_visible`/`tap` can never silently act on invisible content. Set it to `true` only for a deliberate check of an off-screen/invisible node (`assert_not_visible`, `assert_state {visible: false}`, diagnostics).

index.description: Zero-based occurrence among otherwise matching nodes.

TextMatch.description:
A text matching rule: exactly one of `exact`, `contains`, `regex`.

A struct rather than an enum so the agent-facing YAML/JSON form is a plain map (`text: {exact: "Greet"}`) and not a YAML `!tag`.

exact.description: Full string equality (no trimming or normalisation).

VerifyEngine.description:
The execution engine `verify` runs on.

One vocabulary, three front doors: `art` (real ART, or recorded ART evidence with `--reference`) and `rust-vm` (the frozen Rust VM) are the words the `--engine` flag, this schema and the scenario YAML `engine:` field all use.

The scenario field records the engine a scenario was *written for*; it does not select one — the request's `engine` (CLI `--engine`, MCP `engine`) stays authoritative, and a disagreement is reported as `SCENARIO_ENGINE_MISMATCH` in the verdict's `provenance.warnings[]` rather than silently changing the engine. The pre-v0.3 spellings are accepted as aliases (`native-preferred`/`native-only` -> `rust-vm`, `reference-only` -> `art`) with a warning that names the current word.

oneOf.description: Real Google ART through an `acos-art` guest (the default).
The frozen Rust VM / native runtime (diagnostics; never silently chosen).

VerifyRequest.description: `verify`: run an APK + scenario and produce artifacts.

apk.description: APK path (overrides the scenario `app` when set).

artifacts.description:
Artifacts output directory.

A run owns its directory: a non-empty directory written by another run is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the previous run id, unless [`VerifyRequest::overwrite`] is set.

engine.description:
Execution engine: `art` (the default: real ART) or `rust-vm` (the frozen Rust VM).

The default is `art`, qualified by one rule: a request that sets `reference` and omits `engine` replays recorded ART evidence with the `rust-vm` side, because `--reference` is replay, not live ART execution. An explicit `engine: art` together with `reference` is refused (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`), never silently reinterpreted.

flags.description:
Deterministic `NAME=VALUE` flags recorded in the reproducer (`repro.json`'s `flags` and the `--flag` lines of `repro.sh`).

A flag is metadata, not a command-line option: it must be `NAME=VALUE` with a name matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` and a non-empty value, so a value can never be read as another option. A malformed flag is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`details.index` names it).

overwrite.description:
Replace artifacts left by another run in `artifacts` (`--overwrite`).

Off by default: two runs never interleave evidence in one directory, so a stale frame can never be mistaken for this run's.

reference.description: Optional art-reference directory to compare against.

required_fidelity.description: Minimum fidelity the verdict must achieve.
